title: Per-user session files activate only at two or more participants
head: ms-38098d7a:d1
current_summary: Per-user session files are written only when two or more participants are registered. A single configured user stays on the flat file, preserving the solo-first design. Reads discover both layouts, so the split is a write-time change rather than a migration, and an explicit `--user` bypasses the gate.
current_why: Identity and layout are separable: recording who wrote an entry should not force a file split until a second author actually exists. One configured user is declarative intent, not yet multi-user, so waiting for the second participant makes the layout move explicit and mechanical rather than a surprise. Dual-read means the change is reversible without touching history.

title: Skills route through a deterministic registry, and seeded skills are written generic
head: mse_542z3qn0azma9mmx:d1
current_summary: `.memory-seed/skills/index.md` is the deterministic trigger registry: a fresh agent evaluates one map rather than loading every runbook, and new capabilities are routed by adding a registry entry rather than by prose scattered across skills. A skill shipped in the seed is written generic - no hardcoded paths, no machine-specific locations - so it is reusable in any project that installs it.
current_why: Trigger prose inside each skill cannot be evaluated without reading every skill, which is the cost the registry removes; moving trigger logic into `agent-rules.md` was rejected for making the operating contract too large and less extensible. Generic seed content is the same principle applied to the skill body: a runbook carrying one machine's paths is a runbook only that machine can run.

title: Sub-project runtime scoping and inheritance defaults
head: ms-0bd3d8b2:d2
current_summary: A sub-project is a normal folder carrying its own nested `.memory-seed/` runtime, never a folder nested inside the root runtime. The nested runtime scopes work under its containing folder: active state is local by default, detailed session logs stay in the nearest runtime, and parent active state is not read unless the sub-project index explicitly links to it. Parent policy and parent skills are inherited by default; local skill files exist only to override parent behaviour or to hold genuinely local runbooks.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "Detailed session logs remain in the nearest active runtime; parent/root memory gets only" (ms-0bd3d8b2:d2). This decision established the scoping rule that sub-projects keep detailed logs locally while parent gets coordination summaries.

title: Topic sidecar is the topic authority (sidecar > authored > hashtag)
head: mse_8qmv0m07sy95vjm9:d1
current_summary: The topic sidecar is the topic authority, not a derived overlay. Topic resolution follows strict precedence - sidecar attributions first, then the entry's authored `topics:` field, then hashtag and heading axes - instead of unioning sidecar and authored topics. Where an entry has sidecar attributions, those are its topics. Nothing authored is edited or deleted on disk; only which reading a consumer is shown changes, which is what keeps the switch reversible.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "`_topics()` now falls back in order: sidecar `inferred_topics`, then authored `topics:`, then the hashtag/heading axes." (mse_8qmv0m07sy95vjm9:d1). This decision directly establishes the topic priority rule - sidecar authority over authored topics and hashtags.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: `_topics()` now falls back in order: sidecar `inferred_topics`, then authored `topics:`, then the hashtag/heading axes. It unioned the first two until today. - R: JNL's call, and the union stopped being right the moment the two-axis campaign finished. A union is correct while sidecars are sparse ENRICHMENT - an entry tagged `memory-trace` gaining `trail` really is both. It is wrong once the sidecar carries a COMPLETE reading of every decision on two declared axes, because unioning then re-admits the coarse pre-axis label the sweep exists to supersede: an entry reads as `memory-seed` AND `topic-vocabulary` with nothing to say which the corpus currently believes. Measured after the switch: the facet drops `memory-trace` from 204 entries to 76, because entries now answer with the specific slug rather than the root they were parked on. The root is still reachable - `expand_topic_filter` derives it from the child - so nothing lost reach, only false breadth. **Nothing authored is edited, deleted or contradicted on disk.** The entry's own YAML is untouched and still readable as what its author wrote. Only which of the two a READER is shown changed, and that is exactly what makes this reversible. - A: Union and mark provenance in the UI - rejected: it keeps the ambiguity and moves the cost to every consumer. Union only where the sidecar has no area/activity pair - rejected as a rule nobody could predict from the outside. - F: `memory-trace/memory_trace/service.py` (`_topics`), `memory-trace/tests/test_topic_sidecars.py` (assertions inverted, 2 tests added). - T: 225 Trace tests pass. Live facets rebuild to 68 slugs led by `feature-build` 222, `bugfix` 99, `ui-design` 84 - the two-axis reading, not the old one.

live_chain.title: D1 - Use authored sidecars as the only Trace topic truth
live_chain.body: - D: Project entry and decision topics only from their authored topic sidecars; remove link-neighbour topic inference, keep untagged decisions neutral, and let the parent entry expose the deduplicated union of its authored decision topics. - R: Link structure explains relationships, not semantic classification. Inferring colour or community from linked entries made untagged content look authored and obscured which decision actually carried each topic. - A: Retaining inferred linked context as a secondary colour or fallback was rejected because it would continue to present unauthored classification as topic truth. No diagram was added because this is an authority and projection rule without a new spatial or lifecycle topology. - F: `memory-trace/memory_trace/service.py`, `memory-trace/memory_trace/models.py`, `memory-trace/memory_trace/graph_projection.py`, `memory-trace/client/src/App.tsx`, `memory-trace/client/src/graphCommunities.ts`, API contracts, and the authored topic sidecar for `mse_d06t9bccm3yykfqs`. - T: Live Inspector and Graph checks confirmed exact D1/D2 topic attribution and authored communities; untagged decisions remain neutral.
